title: Async TP: pipeline SwiGLU gather

verification.label: Measured TorchTitan async TP · rank 0 CUDA/P2P streams
verification.implementation: TorchTitan v0.2.0 async tensor parallelism with TorchInductor micro-pipeline TP and symmetric memory
verification.workload: Two dense Qwen-shaped layers, hidden 4096, SwiGLU 12288, sequence 4096, BF16, TP=4+SP; displayed scope is L0 gate/up
verification.measurement: 23.412 ms full step; 0.703 ms displayed L0 MLP norm-through-activation window
verification.timeline: Exact rank-0 Nsight kernel and peer-copy timestamps, shifted to the L0 MLP RMSNorm origin.

description: Async TP decomposes an activation all-gather followed by a matmul into peer fetches and rank-local sub-GEMMs. TorchInductor alternates two symmetric CUDA streams so one stream can compute while the other stream fetches or computes another rank chunk.

Build the four measured gate/up chunk envelopes and three peer-to-peer copies. Each compute envelope contains the gate and up projection work for one gathered token chunk; copy-engine transfers are shown on their own lane.

This trace proves overlap, not speedup. For this exact Qwen TP=4 graph, the full async step measured 23.412 ms versus 18.262 ms synchronously: matmul decomposition, barriers, and skipped matmul→reduce-scatter fusion outweighed the hidden copies.
